newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand orders 16 finance firms to merge,consolid.
newsitem.headline: Thailand orders 16 finance firms to merge,consolid.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Friday that it had ordered 16 finance companies to stop operations and submit plans for mergers or consolidations with other parties to authorities in two weeks.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond told a news conference that the companies were suspended because of concerns that their poor financial positions could harm depositors' interests.
Rerngchai added that five strong finance companies would be leaders of the mergers and consolidations that weaker finance firms had been ordered to undertake.
The 16 suspended firms would have to merge with one or more of the five stronger companies.

The central bank planned to grant between two to five new bank licences to major, merged firms, Rerngchai said. Those who could be eligible for the new bank licences would need to have total capital and assets of 150 billion baht ($6 billion).
"We will grant two to five new bank licenses, but we will have to look at granting them on a case by case basis," the governor said.

Those groups of finance firms that merged but failed to obtain new bank licences would be classified as super finance firms that would be allowed to undertake a wider range of financial businesses, he added.

"What we are doing is in line with international standards. I am confident that the measures that we launched and will be implemented are in the right direction," he said. "I believe it will restore foreign investor confidence (in Thailand)."
Thai financial markets have been battered this year by a slowing economy and concerns over the level of bad or poor performing property loans held by banks and finance companies.
